categories.label: Empirical incompleteness
categories.question: What observed phenomena require physics beyond the minimal Standard Model?

categories.label: Theoretical consistency and scope
categories.question: Where does our framework cease to provide an adequate description?

categories.label: Naturalness problems
categories.question: Why do parameters have values that appear unusually sensitive or finely adjusted?

categories.label: Structural and explanatory puzzles
categories.question: Why this particular theory and these parameters?

problems.label: Neutrino masses
problems.include: A mechanism generating nonzero neutrino masses, a model-specific account of the observed mass spectrum, or tests and constraints of that proposed mass mechanism. Seesaw, radiative mass generation, and Dirac mass mechanisms can qualify.
problems.exclude: Merely including neutrinos, assuming measured masses as fixed input, generic neutrino detection, or an isolated lepton-number-violation constraint without a demonstrated connection to this model's neutrino-mass mechanism. Mixing-pattern explanations can additionally qualify as flavor_patterns.

problems.label: Dark matter
problems.include: The model supplies or tests a proposed dark-matter constituent, production mechanism, abundance, stability mechanism, or explanation of dark-matter evidence. Searches or exclusion limits on an explicitly identified dark-matter candidate count.
problems.exclude: A stable or neutral new particle without an explicit dark-matter connection; a dark sector used for another purpose; dark energy; or a background mention of missing matter.

problems.label: Matter–antimatter asymmetry
problems.include: Generation, survival, or a model-specific test of the cosmic baryon asymmetry, including baryogenesis, leptogenesis with a baryon-asymmetry connection, and asymmetric-dark-matter mechanisms tied to baryon asymmetry.
problems.exclude: CP violation, a first-order phase transition, baryon/lepton number violation, or sphalerons alone, without connecting this model to the observed cosmic asymmetry.

problems.label: Quantum gravity
problems.include: A proposed quantum description or unification of gravity, or explicit investigation of whether this model is compatible with quantum gravity, including specific quantum-gravity consistency criteria and realizations.
problems.exclude: Classical gravity, inflation, gravitational waves, or the names string theory/supergravity alone without a substantive quantum-gravity question or construction for this model.

problems.label: Ultraviolet completion
problems.include: A specified higher-energy theory, embedding, or mechanism proposed to complete this model/EFT, remove its high-energy breakdown, or establish a controlled continuum limit. Explicit tests or obstructions to such a completion count.
problems.exclude: The words ultraviolet or renormalizable alone; routine loop renormalization; anomaly cancellation alone; or a high-scale boundary condition with no proposed completion or high-energy adequacy question.

problems.label: Higgs hierarchy
problems.include: A mechanism or quantitative test addressing Higgs/electroweak mass sensitivity to higher scales, stabilization of the electroweak scale, or associated electroweak fine tuning.
problems.exclude: The generic word hierarchy; flavor hierarchies; inflationary scale hierarchies; electroweak symmetry breaking or a Higgs spectrum alone; or an ordinary Higgs correction without an explicit naturalness/stability connection.

problems.label: Strong CP
problems.include: Explaining the small physical QCD theta parameter or testing a proposed solution, such as a QCD axion/Peccei–Quinn mechanism, parity, Nelson–Barr mechanism, or massless-quark proposal.
problems.exclude: CP violation in general; an arbitrary axion-like particle; an electric-dipole-moment bound alone; or a theta term without a model-specific connection to the strong-CP problem.

problems.label: Cosmological constant
problems.include: The smallness, cancellation, radiative stability, or adjustment of gravitational vacuum energy relative to particle-physics scales, including a specific proposed response to the cosmological-constant problem.
problems.exclude: Fitting dark energy, late-time acceleration, quintessence, inflation, or the coincidence problem alone unless the paper explicitly connects the model to the vacuum-energy naturalness problem.

problems.label: Gauge structure
problems.include: An explicit explanation, selection principle, derivation, or emergence of the observed gauge symmetry, its factors, or its breaking pattern. A proposed origin of the Standard Model gauge structure in a larger theory can qualify.
problems.exclude: Merely specifying a gauge group, introducing an extra gauge symmetry, checking anomalies, or choosing a symmetry-breaking chain without investigating why the observed structure follows. Unification does not automatically imply this separate label.

problems.label: Matter representations
problems.include: An explicit explanation or selection of observed fermion/matter representations or charge assignments, including charge quantization, multiplet organization, or a derivation of chiral matter content.
problems.exclude: A field-content table, convenient representation choice, or routine anomaly check alone. Anomaly cancellation qualifies only when used as an explicit explanatory principle for the observed assignments.

problems.label: Three generations
problems.include: A mechanism, constraint, or derivation intended to explain or select the observed number of three fermion generations.
problems.exclude: Assuming three families; introducing three right-handed neutrinos; adding another generation; or explaining family mass differences without addressing the number of generations.

problems.label: Flavor patterns
problems.include: Explaining or predicting observed quark/lepton mass patterns, Yukawa hierarchies, flavor mixing angles, or flavor CP phases through a model-specific structure. Tests of a specified flavor-explanation mechanism count.
problems.exclude: Generic flavor-changing-process bounds, lepton-flavor violation, CP violation, or choosing measured Yukawa parameters as inputs without an explanatory/predictive flavor mechanism. Neutrino mixing textures may also qualify as neutrino_masses only when that separate definition is met.

problems.label: Unification
problems.include: Unifying fundamental gauge interactions, gauge couplings, or quark/lepton multiplets in a common fundamental structure, including quantitative tests of a specified grand-unified construction.
problems.exclude: The name of a GUT group alone; a unified treatment of calculations; or a model jointly addressing neutrino masses and dark matter without fundamental interaction/matter unification.

higgs_hierarchy.rationale: The paper develops the mirror model as a classically scale-invariant framework in which the electroweak scale is generated radiatively and the Higgs is a pseudo-Goldstone boson, explicitly presenting this as a resolution of the hierarchy problem. The viable phenomenological analysis selects the broken-parity case.

evidence.quote: The electroweak scale generated through the dimensional transmutation will be radiatively stable, thus resolving the technical aspect of the hierarchy problem.
We show in section III that this classically scale invariant model is phenomenologically consistent, and also realises the Higgs boson as a PGB of spontaneously broken scale invariance.

evidence.quote: We have demonstrated that this dark matter theory can simply and fully explain the annual modulation signal seen in the DAMA/NaI and DAMA/LIBRA experiments.
our favoured region of parameter space is consistent with the null results of these experiments.

dark_matter.rationale: The review develops mirror matter as asymmetric dark matter, discusses its dark atoms and relic abundance, and examines its cosmological and astrophysical constraints.

evidence.quote: In the mirror DM scenario, dark baryons are bound in heavy mirror atoms due to the mirror nuclear interactions.
The DM today should be in the form of mirror gas and ions plus compact stellar objects.

dark_matter.rationale: The paper explicitly develops mirror matter as a dark-matter candidate and analyzes its density perturbations, processed power spectrum, and constraints relevant to structure formation.

evidence.quote: Mirror matter is a dark matter candidate. In this paper, we re-examine the linear regime of density perturbation growth in a universe containing mirror dark matter.
Observations require us to take the mirror baryons to dominate the total present-day matter density
evidence.locator: L000454–L000457; Section II, Cosmology with mirror dark matter

mechanisms.label: Higgs/BEH mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: Scalar-field vacuum expectation values break a gauge symmetry and generate masses for gauge bosons and, through Yukawa couplings, fermions.
mechanisms.include: The model's Higgs or BEH sector is explicitly used to generate masses or implement the relevant spontaneous gauge-symmetry breaking.
mechanisms.exclude: A Higgs field or Higgs portal alone, an assumed mass term, or a generic reference to electroweak symmetry breaking without this mass-generation role.

mechanisms.label: Coleman–Weinberg mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: Quantum corrections generate a symmetry-breaking vacuum even when the classical potential does not.
mechanisms.include: The paper explicitly derives or uses symmetry breaking generated by the radiatively corrected effective potential, including classically scale-invariant realizations.
mechanisms.exclude: Ordinary loop corrections without radiatively induced symmetry breaking; running couplings or scale generation alone without an evidenced symmetry-breaking vacuum.

mechanisms.label: Dynamical symmetry breaking
mechanisms.main_idea: Strong dynamics or a condensate, rather than an elementary scalar vacuum expectation value, spontaneously breaks a symmetry and can generate masses.
mechanisms.include: A specified nonperturbative or strong-interaction condensate is explicitly responsible for symmetry breaking or mass generation.
mechanisms.exclude: An elementary Higgs mechanism, strong dynamics with no stated breaking or mass-generation role, or generic use of the word dynamical.

mechanisms.label: Stueckelberg mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: A gauge field acquires a gauge-invariant mass through a compensating scalar degree of freedom and its shift transformation, without a conventional Higgs condensate being required.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly uses a Stueckelberg field or equivalent compensator to provide a gauge-boson mass while maintaining gauge invariance.
mechanisms.exclude: A massive vector alone, a Proca mass without the compensator construction, or a conventional Higgs-generated vector mass.

mechanisms.label: Type-I seesaw
mechanisms.main_idea: Heavy gauge-singlet right-handed neutrinos with Majorana masses induce small active-neutrino masses after electroweak symmetry breaking.
mechanisms.include: Evidence identifies the singlet-fermion seesaw structure and its induced light-neutrino masses.
mechanisms.exclude: A right-handed or sterile neutrino by itself, a generic Majorana mass, or a seesaw label inferred from a model name without structural evidence.

mechanisms.label: Type-II seesaw
mechanisms.main_idea: A scalar electroweak triplet couples to lepton pairs and generates small Majorana neutrino masses through its induced vacuum expectation value.
mechanisms.include: Evidence connects the scalar electroweak triplet and its lepton coupling or induced vacuum expectation value to Majorana neutrino mass generation.
mechanisms.exclude: A scalar triplet alone, scalar-mediated processes without the neutrino-mass role, or type inferred from the model name alone.

mechanisms.label: Type-III seesaw
mechanisms.main_idea: Heavy fermions in an electroweak triplet induce small active-neutrino masses through mixing after electroweak symmetry breaking.
mechanisms.include: Evidence identifies the fermion-triplet seesaw structure and its contribution to neutrino masses.
mechanisms.exclude: An electroweak fermion triplet alone, or type inferred from a model name without structural evidence.

mechanisms.label: Inverse seesaw
mechanisms.main_idea: A small lepton-number-violating parameter in an extended singlet-fermion sector suppresses active-neutrino masses, allowing relatively low new-physics scales.
mechanisms.include: The small neutrino masses are explicitly tied to the inverse-seesaw mass matrix and its small lepton-number-violating parameter.
mechanisms.exclude: Sterile neutrinos or a low-scale seesaw alone without the characteristic small-parameter structure.

mechanisms.label: Linear seesaw
mechanisms.main_idea: Small active-neutrino masses arise from a term linear in the small lepton-number-violating parameter in an extended neutral-fermion mass matrix.
mechanisms.include: Evidence explicitly identifies the linear-seesaw mass-matrix contribution as the source of neutrino masses.
mechanisms.exclude: A generic low-scale seesaw or sterile-neutrino model without the linear-seesaw structure.

mechanisms.label: Radiative neutrino mass
mechanisms.main_idea: Neutrino masses are generated by specified loop diagrams involving new fields and interactions; representative families include Zee, Zee–Babu, and scotogenic models.
mechanisms.include: The paper explicitly identifies a loop-level mechanism as the origin of neutrino masses, including Zee, Zee–Babu, scotogenic, or another specified radiative neutrino-mass construction.
mechanisms.exclude: Generic loop corrections to an already present neutrino mass, loop-induced observables unrelated to neutrino-mass origin, or the mere presence of fields used in a known radiative model.

mechanisms.label: GIM mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: Flavor-changing neutral currents are suppressed by cancellation among contributions from members of quark multiplets, with residual effects controlled by mass differences and mixing.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly invokes or realizes GIM cancellation to suppress flavor-changing neutral currents.
mechanisms.exclude: Flavor constraints or small flavor-changing rates without the cancellation mechanism.

mechanisms.label: Kobayashi–Maskawa mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: A complex phase in the quark mixing matrix permits CP violation in the quark sector when there are at least three generations.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly attributes quark-sector CP violation to the complex Kobayashi–Maskawa mixing structure or studies its realization.
mechanisms.exclude: A CKM matrix used only as input, generic CP violation, or lepton-sector CP violation without the quark mixing mechanism.

mechanisms.label: Froggatt–Nielsen mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: A flavor symmetry broken by a flavon generates hierarchical effective Yukawa couplings through higher-dimensional operators suppressed by a heavy scale.
mechanisms.include: A flavor charge assignment and symmetry-breaking flavon or equivalent spurion are explicitly used to generate Yukawa or fermion-mass hierarchies.
mechanisms.exclude: Hierarchical Yukawas assumed as input, generic flavor symmetries, or flavons without the stated hierarchy-generating role.

mechanisms.label: MSW mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: Matter effects alter neutrino propagation and can produce resonant flavor conversion as the effective mixing conditions change in a medium.
mechanisms.include: The model or analysis explicitly uses matter-enhanced neutrino flavor conversion, including the Mikheyev–Smirnov–Wolfenstein resonance.
mechanisms.exclude: Vacuum neutrino oscillations, matter effects without flavor conversion, or a generic mention of neutrino propagation in matter.

mechanisms.label: Peccei–Quinn mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: A global chiral symmetry dynamically relaxes the effective QCD theta angle; its spontaneous breaking yields an axion.
mechanisms.include: A Peccei–Quinn symmetry and its QCD-anomalous breaking are explicitly used to address strong CP, whether or not the axion is the paper's focus.
mechanisms.exclude: An arbitrary axion-like particle, a global symmetry without the strong-CP role, or axion phenomenology not tied to Peccei–Quinn dynamics.

mechanisms.label: Nelson–Barr mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: CP is exact in the fundamental theory and spontaneously broken in a structured way that permits weak-sector CP violation while keeping the strong-CP phase naturally small at tree level.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly implements the Nelson–Barr structure to solve the strong-CP problem.
mechanisms.exclude: Spontaneous CP violation or vector-like quarks alone, without the structure and strong-CP objective.

mechanisms.label: Leptogenesis
mechanisms.main_idea: A lepton asymmetry is generated and partly converted into baryon asymmetry, typically through electroweak sphaleron processes.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly generates a lepton asymmetry with a connection to the cosmic baryon asymmetry, including thermal and nonthermal variants.
mechanisms.exclude: Lepton-number violation or CP violation alone, or an asymmetry with no stated connection to baryon production.

mechanisms.label: Electroweak baryogenesis
mechanisms.main_idea: Baryon asymmetry is generated around the electroweak transition using CP-violating dynamics and baryon-number-violating sphaleron processes, with conditions that preserve the asymmetry.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly produces the cosmic baryon asymmetry during or associated with electroweak symmetry breaking or its phase transition.
mechanisms.exclude: A first-order electroweak phase transition, new CP violation, or sphalerons alone without the electroweak baryogenesis account.

mechanisms.label: Affleck–Dine mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: A scalar field carrying baryon or lepton number develops a large early-universe condensate whose out-of-equilibrium evolution generates an asymmetry.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly uses the evolution or decay of a baryonic/leptonic scalar condensate to generate the cosmic asymmetry.
mechanisms.exclude: Scalar condensates or supersymmetric flat directions without this asymmetry-generating role.

mechanisms.label: GUT baryogenesis
mechanisms.main_idea: Baryon asymmetry is generated by out-of-equilibrium decays or interactions of grand-unified states with baryon-number violation and CP violation.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly connects GUT-scale states or interactions to generation of the cosmic baryon asymmetry.
mechanisms.exclude: A GUT model, baryon-number violation, or heavy-particle decays without the baryogenesis connection.

mechanisms.label: Akhmedov–Rubakov–Smirnov (ARS) mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: Coherent oscillations and CP-violating interactions of GeV-scale or otherwise relativistic sterile neutrinos generate flavor asymmetries before equilibration, which can yield baryon asymmetry.
mechanisms.include: The paper explicitly identifies sterile-neutrino oscillation leptogenesis of the ARS type, including flavor asymmetries and their baryon-asymmetry connection.
mechanisms.exclude: Sterile neutrinos or leptogenesis without the characteristic oscillation-driven ARS dynamics.

mechanisms.label: Thermal freeze-out
mechanisms.main_idea: A dark-matter species once in thermal equilibrium becomes chemically decoupled as expansion outpaces number-changing reactions, leaving a relic abundance.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly explains or tests the dark-matter abundance through thermal equilibrium followed by freeze-out.
mechanisms.exclude: A thermal relic label without the model-specific freeze-out account, or abundance from freeze-in, misalignment, or another production mechanism alone.

mechanisms.label: Freeze-in
mechanisms.main_idea: A feebly interacting dark-matter species is gradually produced from the thermal bath or decays of bath particles and never reaches thermal equilibrium.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly identifies out-of-equilibrium accumulation of dark matter through feeble interactions as its production and abundance mechanism.
mechanisms.exclude: Generic nonthermal production or a weakly coupled dark sector without the freeze-in abundance account.

mechanisms.label: Misalignment mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: A light field displaced from its potential minimum begins coherent oscillations as the universe evolves, contributing a cold relic abundance.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly uses initial field displacement and subsequent coherent evolution to produce the dark-matter relic abundance.
mechanisms.exclude: An axion or scalar dark-matter candidate without misalignment production, or an unrelated coherent condensate.

mechanisms.label: Coannihilation
mechanisms.main_idea: A dark-matter particle's relic abundance is set in part by annihilations involving a nearly degenerate, thermally populated partner species.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly relies on near-degenerate partner states and their annihilations to determine the dark-matter relic abundance.
mechanisms.exclude: A partner particle or mass degeneracy alone, or annihilations that do not affect the dark-matter abundance.

mechanisms.label: Asymmetric dark matter
mechanisms.main_idea: A particle–antiparticle asymmetry in the dark sector sets or substantially contributes to the dark-matter abundance, often with a relation to the visible baryon asymmetry.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly uses a dark particle–antiparticle asymmetry to determine the surviving dark-matter relic abundance; generation or transfer of that asymmetry may be studied or assumed as an initial condition.
mechanisms.exclude: Unequal populations with no connection to relic abundance, or a baryon asymmetry with no dark-sector abundance link.

mechanisms.label: Dimensional transmutation
mechanisms.main_idea: A dimensionless coupling is traded for a dynamically generated dimensionful scale through renormalization-group running or a related quantum effect.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly generates a physical scale from dimensionless parameters through running or quantum dynamics.
mechanisms.exclude: A scale inserted as a parameter, ordinary running without scale generation, or a Coleman–Weinberg label inferred solely from dimensional transmutation (and vice versa).

mechanisms.label: Little Higgs / collective symmetry breaking
mechanisms.main_idea: The Higgs is a pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone boson protected by multiple symmetries such that no single coupling breaks all protective symmetries, postponing large radiative mass corrections.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly implements collective symmetry breaking to protect a pseudo-Goldstone Higgs and address electroweak-scale sensitivity.
mechanisms.exclude: A pseudo-Goldstone scalar or extended Higgs sector without collective protection of the Higgs mass.

mechanisms.label: Twin Higgs
mechanisms.main_idea: An approximate exchange or larger global symmetry makes the Higgs a pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone boson and cancels leading radiative sensitivity through partner sectors that need not carry Standard Model color.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly uses the twin-symmetry structure and partner contributions to protect the Higgs mass.
mechanisms.exclude: A hidden or mirror sector alone, or Higgs partners without the symmetry-based protection mechanism.

mechanisms.label: Relaxion mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: A slowly evolving field scans the Higgs mass parameter during cosmological evolution and becomes trapped when Higgs-dependent barriers arise, selecting a small electroweak scale.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly implements cosmological scanning and Higgs-dependent stopping or trapping to address the electroweak hierarchy.
mechanisms.exclude: A rolling scalar, scanning of unrelated parameters, or a Higgs-dependent potential without the hierarchy-selection mechanism.

mechanisms.label: Giudice–Masiero mechanism
mechanisms.main_idea: In supergravity, a Higgs bilinear in the Kähler potential induces an effective supersymmetric Higgs mass parameter after supersymmetry breaking.
mechanisms.include: The model explicitly uses a Kähler-potential operator and supersymmetry breaking to generate the effective Higgs μ parameter.
mechanisms.exclude: A μ parameter simply inserted into the superpotential, generic supersymmetry breaking, or a Kähler operator without the stated μ-generation role.
